definitions.definition: The force or the component of a force which a surface exerts on an object with which it is in contact, and which is perpendicular to the surface.
distractors: The force that opposes the motion of a moving object relative to a surface.
The gravitational force the Earth exerts on any object on or near its surface.
The force which opposes the tendency of motion of a stationary object relative to a surface.
The force applied to an object by a person or another object.
The force transmitted through a string, rope, or wire when it is pulled tight.
The force that acts parallel to a surface when an object is in contact with it.

definitions.definition: The force that opposes the motion of an object and which acts parallel to the surface.
distractors: The force which a surface exerts on an object perpendicular to the surface.
The attractive force between two masses.
The force that accelerates an object downwards.
The resistance of an object to any change in its state of motion.
The force exerted on a freely falling body.
The tension in a rope connecting two moving objects.

definitions.definition: The force that opposes the tendency of motion of a stationary object relative to a surface.
distractors: The force that opposes the motion of a moving object relative to a surface.

The constant force acting on an object sliding on a rough surface.
The normal force exerted by a horizontal surface.

definitions.definition: The force that opposes the motion of a moving object relative to a surface.

When object A exerts a force on object B, object B simultaneously exerts an oppositely directed force of equal magnitude on object A.

The resistance of an object to any change in its state of motion.

definitions.definition: The resistance of an object to any change in its state of motion.
distractors: The product of an object's mass and its velocity.

The tendency of an object to accelerate when a net force is applied.

The property of a moving object to eventually come to a stop.

The total energy of an isolated system remains constant.

definitions.definition: The gravitational force, in newton (N), exerted by the Earth on an object.
distractors: The amount of matter in a body, measured in kilograms.
The resistance of an object to a change in its state of motion.
The force exerted by a surface on an object in contact with it.
The constant acceleration of an object in free fall.

definitions.definition: The amount of matter in a body measured in kilogram (kg).
distractors: The gravitational force exerted by the Earth on an object.
The weight of an object on a given planet.
The force required to accelerate an object at $1 \text{ m\cdot s}^{-2}$.
A measure of an object's velocity.

definitions.definition: The sensation experienced when all contact forces are removed.
distractors: The condition when there is no gravitational force acting on an object.

proportionality.statement: According to Newton's Second Law, the acceleration of an object is...
proportionality.correct: directly proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to its mass.
distractors: directly proportional to its mass and inversely proportional to the net force.
directly proportional to both the net force and its mass.
inversely proportional to both the net force and its mass.
independent of its mass but directly proportional to the net force.
constant as long as the applied force remains constant, regardless of mass.
directly proportional to the square of the net force.

proportionality.statement: If the net force acting on an object is doubled while its mass remains constant, its acceleration will...
distractors: halve.
quadruple.
remain the same.
decrease by a factor of four.
increase exponentially.
become zero.

proportionality.statement: If the mass of an object is doubled while the net force acting on it remains constant, its acceleration will...
distractors: double.
quadruple.
remain the same.

become zero.

remains the same.

distractors: becomes half ($1/2$) of the original force.

concepts.question: Which of the following is TRUE about action-reaction pairs according to Newton's Third Law?
concepts.correct: They act on different objects and therefore cannot cancel each other out.
distractors: They act on the same object and cancel each other out, resulting in a net force of zero.
They only exist if the objects are moving at constant velocity.
The reaction force occurs slightly after the action force is applied.
They exist between two objects only when there is direct physical contact.
The larger mass exerts a larger action force than the reaction force it experiences.
They are responsible for keeping an object at rest according to the First Law.

concepts.question: An object moves at a constant velocity on a horizontal surface. What can be concluded about the forces acting on it?
concepts.correct: The net force acting on the object is zero.
distractors: There are no forces acting on the object.
The applied force is greater than the frictional force.
The normal force is greater than the weight of the object.
The object has no inertia.
The frictional force is zero.
A constant net force must be acting in the direction of motion.

concepts.question: When an elevator accelerates upwards, a person standing on a scale inside it will notice that their apparent weight...
concepts.correct: is greater than their true weight.
distractors: is less than their true weight.
is exactly equal to their true weight.
is zero (weightlessness).
decreases as the acceleration increases.
depends only on the velocity, not the acceleration.
is equal to the normal force minus the applied force.

concepts.question: When an elevator is in free fall, a person standing on a scale inside it will notice that the scale reading is...
concepts.correct: zero, because the normal force is zero.
distractors: equal to their true weight.
greater than their true weight.
equal to their mass.
decreasing at a constant rate.
equal to the gravitational constant $G$.
negative.
